title: Senior Manager, International Reporting
description: Our mission at Oura is to empower every person to own their inner potential. Our award-winning products help our global community gain a deeper knowledge of their readiness, activity, and sleep quality by using their Oura Ring and its connected app. We've helped millions of people understand and improve their health by providing daily insights and practical steps to inspire healthy lifestyles. Empowering the world starts with living our values and empowering our team. As a quickly growing company focused on helping people live healthier and happier lives, we ensure that our team members have what they need to do their best work — both in and out of the office.  We are looking for a Senior Manager, International Reporting to build and lead the function that owns the accuracy and compliance of Oura's international entities: statutory reporting, sustainability (ESG) reporting, and the entity-level technical accounting that ties our global structure together. You'll join the Global Financial Reporting team, reporting to the Senior Director, Global Financial Reporting, Technical Accounting, SOX & Equity Admin, and partner closely with Tax, Treasury, Legal, FP&A, Controllership, and our SOX and Internal Audit partners. What You Will Do: Own end-to-end statutory reporting for Oura's international entities, including timetables, preparation and review of local financial statements, audits, and filings, working with local teams and service providers Serve as the primary point of contact for statutory auditors across entities and drive timely audit completion and resolution of findings Prepare and review US GAAP to local GAAP / IFRS adjustments by entity, and keep the entity compliance calendar current as local requirements change Lead Oura's sustainability reporting obligations, including California reporting and first-year CSRD reporting, and build the data, process, and control foundation for ESG reporting Own technical accounting for the international entity structure, including functional currency determinations, foreign currency remeasurement and translation (ASC 830), and CTA Oversee intercompany accounting policy and processes, including reconciliations, settlements, and eliminations, in alignment with transfer pricing agreements (with Tax) Advise on the accounting and reporting impacts of new entities, restructurings, and ERP and globalization initiatives, and drive standardization and automation across international close and reporting Design and maintain internal controls over international reporting with the SOX team, and build and develop the team as the function scales This is a remote US role. You'll work closely with colleagues in Europe, including regular early-morning meetings. This is a remote role based in the US. What you'll bring 10+ years of progressive accounting experience, including Big 4 or national firm experience and multinational industry experience Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance and an active CPA (international equivalents such as CA or ACCA considered) Deep knowledge of US GAAP, working knowledge of IFRS and local GAAP frameworks (e.g., Finnish FAS), and proven experience owning statutory reporting across multiple jurisdictions Strong technical expertise in foreign currency, intercompany, consolidations, and transfer pricing coordination Experience with sustainability reporting (CSRD/ESRS, ISSB, or similar) and with ERP and consolidation systems (e.g., NetSuite, OneStream, Workiva), strongly preferred Clear communication with non-accounting partners and senior leadership, and a track record of building processes, controls, and teams in a high-growth environment Benefits At Ōura, we care about you and your well-being. Everyone here at Ōura has a ring of their own and we are continually looking to improve employee health. What we offer: Competitive salary and equity packages Health, dental, vision insurance, and mental health resources An Ōura Ring of your own plus employee discounts for friends & family 20 days of paid time off plus 13 paid holidays plus 8 days of flexible wellness time off Paid sick leave and parental leave Ōura takes a market-based approach to pay, which may vary depending on your location. US locations are categorized into tiers based on a cost of labor index for that geographic area. While most offers will be closer to the starting range, successful candidates' pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location, internal peer equity, and market conditions. These ranges may be modified in the future. Region 1 $170,000 - $200,000 Region 2 $154,700 - $182,000 Region 3 $139,400 - $164,000 A recruiter can determine your Region based on your US location. We are not considering candidates residing in the following states: Alaska (AK), Delaware (DE), Iowa (IA), Mississippi (MS), Nebraska (NE), South Dakota (SD), West Virginia (WV), and Wisconsin (WI). Oura is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

title: SEC Reporting - Vice President
description: About the Role iCapital is looking to hire a Vice President to join the Corporate Reporting team within Corporate Finance. Reporting to the Senior Vice President, SEC Reporting, this individual will be a key leader across building out the firm’s SOX controls readiness program as well as focus on iCapital's technical accounting programs. This role combines hands-on experience with business process controls and IT general controls (ITGCs), public-company reporting and governance requirements, and complex U.S. GAAP technical accounting matters. This individual will partner closely with other members of the Corporate Finance, Corporate Development, Technology, Legal and Compliance, Human Resources and Benefits teams. This role also works with outsourced advisors for technical accounting and tax, external auditors, and other business leaders to build scalable, audit-ready processes and help prepare the organization to operate like a public company. Responsibilities Lead key workstreams within the firm-wide SOX program, including risk assessment, scoping, control design, documentation, testing coordination, deficiency evaluation, remediation, and executive reporting. Provide subject matter expertise across both business process controls and ITGCs, including the evaluation of control dependencies, automated controls, system-generated reports, and key interfaces. Help design and execute the organization’s path to SOX compliance, including readiness planning, external auditor coordination, evidence standards, testing strategy, and sustainable program governance. Partner with process and control owners to develop and maintain process narratives, flowcharts, risk and control matrices, and other control documentation. Identify control gaps and process improvement opportunities, develop practical remediation plans, and drive issues through timely and sustainable resolution. Provide periodic reporting to senior management, including the CAO and CFO, on SOX readiness, testing results, remediation status, emerging risks, and key decisions. Lead and support initiatives across accounting, financial reporting, internal controls, governance, and SEC reporting capabilities. Prepare and review technical accounting memoranda for complex and judgmental matters, including business combinations, asset acquisitions, revenue recognition, stock-based compensation, consolidation, capital raising activity and other transactions. Research and assess new accounting standards and SEC developments, determine their impact, and coordinate implementation across relevant stakeholders. Develop and maintain accounting policies that translate U.S. GAAP and SEC requirements into clear, scalable operating practices. Support financial statement preparation and review, including U.S. GAAP and SEC disclosure requirements, as needed. Mentor team members and strengthen technical accounting, controls, project management, and executive communication capabilities across the organization. Qualifications 8+ years of progressive public accounting, internal controls, financial reporting, or technical accounting experience Public accounting experience is required   CPA license is required Demonstrated experience testing or evaluating internal controls at a public company, including both business process controls and ITGCs Experience helping a company prepare for or complete its first year of Section 404(b) auditor attestation is strongly preferred Strong knowledge of U.S. GAAP, SEC reporting requirements, PCAOB standards, and public-company internal control expectations Able to research complex accounting matters, develop well-supported conclusions, and prepare clear technical accounting memoranda Financial services, fintech, asset management, wealth management, or alternative investments experience is preferred Proven ability to lead cross-functional programs, influence senior stakeholders, prioritize competing demands, and drive workstreams to completion Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical matters into concise, decision-oriented recommendations Highly organized and detail-oriented and able to connect detailed execution to broader business objectives Benefits The base salary range for this role is $150,000 to $175,000.  iCapital offers a compensation package which includes salary, equity for all full-time employees, and an annual performance bonus. Employees also receive a comprehensive benefits package that includes an employer matched retirement plan, generously subsidized healthcare with 100% employer paid dental, vision, telemedicine, and virtual mental health counseling, parental leave, and unlimited paid time off (PTO). We believe the best ideas and innovation happen when we are together. Employees in this role will work in the office Monday-Thursday, with the flexibility to work remotely on Friday. For additional information on iCapital, please visit https://www.icapitalnetwork.com/about-us

title: Senior SOX Manager - Business Processes
description: We're transforming the grocery industry At Instacart, we invite the world to share love through food because we believe everyone should have access to the food they love and more time to enjoy it together. Where others see a simple need for grocery delivery, we see exciting complexity and endless opportunity to serve the varied needs of our community. We work to deliver an essential service that customers rely on to get their groceries and household goods, while also offering safe and flexible earnings opportunities to Instacart Personal Shoppers. Instacart has become a lifeline for millions of people, and we’re building the team to help push our shopping cart forward. If you’re ready to do the best work of your life, come join our table. Instacart is a Flex First team There’s no one-size fits all approach to how we do our best work. Our employees have the flexibility to choose where they do their best work—whether it’s from home, an office, or your favorite coffee shop—while staying connected and building community through regular in-person events. Learn more about our flexible approach to where we work. Why this role is on the menu The SOX Senior Manager, Business Processes will assume ownership of the business process side of Instacart's SOX compliance program, leading risk assessments, managing control testing, and resolving deficiencies across key financial and operational processes.    Reporting to SOX Compliance leadership, this role collaborates closely with accounting, finance, operations, IT, and external auditors, and serves as a trusted advisor to process owners across Revenue Operations, procurement, legal, and engineering to ensure controls are integrated into business processes and system workflows.    The team is committed to developing an effective control environment that supports transparency and accountability in financial reporting, and this role will provide the thought leadership on governance, process optimization, and risk transformation across finance and revenue systems needed to get there.   What you'll cook up in your first year The end-to-end SOX compliance program for business processes is owned and operated effectively, with control scoping, documentation, rationalization, and deficiency remediation completed in alignment with SOX 404 requirements and external auditor reliance strategies. Risk assessments across high-risk processes including procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, inventory management, and revenue lifecycle (aligned with ASC 606) are completed, with ICFR controls designed, validated, and tested for operating effectiveness. Control deficiencies are identified, evaluated, and remediated through close partnership with process owners across accounting, operations, procurement, and legal, with corrective actions defined and tracked to closure. Cross-functional alignment is established across finance, accounting, RevOps, and engineering to embed controls into system and process workflows, with technology solutions identified to automate manual processes and improve control effectiveness. SOX status updates, risk assessments, and remediation progress are consistently prepared and presented to the SOX Quarterly Steering Committee, Quarterly Audit Committee, Quarterly Disclosure Committee, and Quarterly External Audit Close Meetings.   The secret ingredients we're looking for Must-have pantry staples (Minimum Qualifications) Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field; CPA, CIA, or equivalent certification is highly preferred 10 years of experience in SOX compliance, internal audit, or related fields, with a focus on business processes. Strong understanding of SOX 404 requirements, COSO framework, and US GAAP. Proven success in designing and testing controls for operational and financial processes, including procure-to-pay, order-to-cash, inventory management, and financial reporting; experience designing control frameworks within finance systems, beyond traditional audit. Exceptional communication and collaboration skills to work effectively with cross-functional teams and senior leadership. Strong problem-solving and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.   Optional garnishes (Preferred Qualifications) Master's degree (MBA, Accounting, or a related field) is a plus. Experience working in a publicly traded company or with a Big Four accounting firm. Familiarity with ERP systems such as Oracle, SAP, Workday, etc., revenue/billing platforms (e.g., Salesforce CPQ/Billing, Stripe) including custom or internally built revenue systems, and experience supporting control audits for these systems. Proven ability to evaluate and implement process improvements and automation solutions. Experience working in a fast-paced, high-growth, or complex organizational environment. Strong experience in revenue accounting (ASC 606) within complex environments, including subscription, multi-element arrangements,

title: Senior Risk Manager – Technology & Enterprise Operations
description: This is a Buffalo, NY based position requiring onsite work four days a week, with the flexibility to work from home one day a week. Senior Risk Manager – Technology & Enterprise Operations The Senior Risk Manager is a key member of the Technology & Enterprise Operations First Line Risk team, serving as the primary risk advisor to various consumer lending operations and technology domains, including Retail Servicing, Customer Asset Management (CAM), and Consumer, Business & Retail Banking Technology. In this role, you will build trusted partnerships with business leaders, Front Office Risk Officers, and cross-functional stakeholders to proactively identify, assess, and manage operational, technology, regulatory, and emerging risks. The successful candidate will champion a culture of continuous risk advisement, embedding risk-informed decision making into business processes, strategic initiatives, and day-to-day operations rather than relying on reactive risk management practices. The successful candidate will lead and execute multiple risk initiatives, drive effective governance and reporting practices, enhance risk frameworks and controls, and ensure alignment with the Bank's risk appetite and regulatory expectations. This position is responsible for influencing risk-informed decision making, promoting operational resilience, and strengthening sustainable risk management practices across the organization. Primary Responsibilities Serve as the primary risk advisor to assigned Technology & Enterprise Operations business lines, providing strategic guidance on operational, technology, compliance, regulatory, and emerging risks. Build trusted partnerships with Operations leadership, frontline Risk Officers, and cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen risk awareness and decision-making. Promote a culture of proactive risk advisement, embedding risk considerations into business processes, initiatives, and strategic planning activities. Lead risk assessments and evaluate controls to identify opportunities to mitigate risk, enhance governance, and improve operational effectiveness. Drive multiple risk initiatives and remediation efforts, ensuring timely execution and sustainable outcomes. Develop and maintain meaningful risk reporting, metrics, and Key Risk Indicators (KRIs) that provide actionable insights to senior management. Partner with business and risk teams to ensure compliance with applicable regulatory requirements, policies, and enterprise risk management standards. Prepare and present risk-related reporting and recommendations to senior leadership and governance committees. Identify opportunities to streamline processes, strengthen controls, and improve efficiency across risk management activities. Support audit, regulatory, and issue management activities, ensuring timely resolution of findings and adherence to internal control standards. Provide leadership, coaching, and guidance to risk professionals and project teams as applicable. Promote an environment that supports belonging and reflects the M&T Bank brand. Scope of Responsibilities This position provides risk leadership and oversight across designated Technology & Enterprise Operations business domains, including various consumer lending operations and technology domains, including Retail Servicing, Customer Asset Management, and Consumer, Business & Retail Banking Technology. The role partners extensively with senior business leaders, frontline Risk Officers, Compliance, Audit, and other Risk Management functions to ensure effective risk governance, operational resilience, and strategic alignment with enterprise risk objectives. Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities Lead and develop a team of four or more risk professionals. Responsible for establishing the strategic direction of the function and building organizational capabilities to support a growing risk advisory model, with potential expansion of the team as business needs evolve. Education and Experience Required Bachelor's degree and a minimum of nine years of experience in Risk Management, Operations, Audit, Compliance, or a related discipline. Demonstrated experience providing risk advisory support to business leaders and cross-functional teams in a highly regulated environment. Experience leading complex initiatives and influencing stakeholders across multiple business functions. Strong understanding of risk management frameworks, governance practices, regulatory expectations, and internal controls. Exceptional verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively engage audiences at all organizational levels. title: Technology & Cyber Risk, VP
description: Who We Are Enterprise Technology Risk Management (ETRM) is part of State Street’s Enterprise Risk Management organization. As a Second Line of Defense function, ETRM provides independent oversight, monitoring, effective challenge, and guidance related to technology and cybersecurity risk. Who We Are Looking For We are seeking an experienced Cyber & Technology Risk Vice President to serve as the primary technology risk partner for State Street’s newly established Wealth Services business. This is a hands-on role responsible for coordinating and managing cyber and technology risk oversight activities for Wealth Services. The successful candidate will work closely with Wealth Services Risk Management, business leaders, technology teams, and other risk partners to identify, assess, monitor, challenge, escalate, and report technology and cybersecurity risks. The ideal candidate will bring more than 10 years of experience in Technology and Cybersecurity Risk, including experience within Wealth Management. Strong knowledge of technology and operational resilience is also important. Candidates may come from first-line Technology Risk, second-line risk oversight, or Technology Audit, provided they have direct experience assessing and challenging technology and cybersecurity risks. This role requires someone who can independently manage complex risk activities, communicate effectively with senior stakeholders, and translate technical issues into clear business and risk implications. Why This Role Is Important to Us Wealth Services is a new strategic business for State Street. This newly created role offers the opportunity to help establish and mature its cyber and technology risk oversight capabilities as the business, technology environment, and risk profile continue to develop. As the primary ETRM contact for Wealth Services, the successful candidate will provide independent oversight and effective challenge while helping the business identify and manage technology, cybersecurity, and resilience risks. The role will also support clear risk reporting to senior management, governance committees, and other stakeholders. What You Will Be Responsible For As Cyber & Technology Risk, Vice President – Wealth Services, you will: Serve as the primary ETRM point of contact for the Wealth Services business and its Risk Management team. title: Senior AML/CFT Compliance Officer
description: RULEMATCH has built a digital assets trading and clearing venue with world-class partners to meet the specific needs of regulated financial institutions. By offering significantly more capital-efficient and lower latency trading, RULEMATCH is helping increase institutional adoption and enable the next evolution of the crypto and digital asset market. To strengthen our compliance function, RULEMATCH AG, based in Zürich, Switzerland, is looking for a Senior AML/CFT Compliance Officer . In this role, you will play a key part in ensuring the effectiveness and ongoing development of RULEMATCH’s AML/CFT framework. You will combine hands-on compliance expertise with sound regulatory judgement, taking ownership of key compliance processes and contributing to a robust control environment in a dynamic and evolving regulatory landscape. Tasks Take ownership of the ongoing monitoring, maintenance and enhancement of the AML/CFT framework to ensure compliance with applicable legal and regulatory requirements. Develop, draft, review and maintain internal AML/CFT policies, procedures and controls. Oversee and perform AML/CFT compliance operations, including participant onboarding, KYC and due diligence. Ensure appropriate documentation and lifecycle management of participant relationships. Review and investigate transaction monitoring and screening alerts, assess potentially suspicious activities and ensure appropriate escalation and documentation. Assess the effectiveness of existing AML/CFT controls and drive continuous improvement of processes, systems and risk mitigation measures. Support regulatory matters, including the preparation of documentation, responses and information required by supervisory authorities. Collaborate with internal stakeholders to embed a strong compliance culture and deliver AML/CFT training across the organisation. Requirements Several years of relevant professional experience in AML/CFT compliance, ideally within financial services, banking, digital assets or fintech. Strong knowledge of AML/CFT regulatory requirements and their practical application within a regulated financial institution. Experience in developing and maintaining compliance frameworks, assessing regulatory risks and implementing effective controls. Experience in engaging with supervisory authorities or supporting regulatory examinations and enquiries is a strong advantage. Experience with digital assets, digital securities and related technologies is a plus. Excellent written and spoken German and English are mandatory. Strong professional judgement, integrity and the ability to take ownership of complex compliance matters and make sound, risk-based decisions. A pragmatic, business-oriented and detail-conscious approach, combined with an entrepreneurial mindset. The ability to operate independently in a fast-paced environment, manage competing priorities and work flexibly when required. An open-minded, solution-oriented attitude, strong communication skills and a collaborative mindset. A genuine interest in technology and in optimising compliance systems, processes and technical implementations. Benefits Annual salary of CHF 150’000 and additional stock appreciation rights to participate in the increase in value of the company. Be part of a venture in a fast-growing market with the ambition to compete with the world's best. Inspiring environment with a focus on excellence, teamwork, and transparency.
